headline: Kotor: a walled Venetian town on Europe's southernmost fjord-like bay, with seafood, stone villages and mountain views
summary: Kotor sits at the head of the Bay of Kotor, a UNESCO-listed bay in Montenegro. Expect a medieval old town, a steep fortress climb, baroque Perast with its island churches, and seafood konobas. Montenegro uses the euro. Tivat is the closest airport, about 15-20 minutes away, and Dubrovnik is the main alternative. Searches were thin on prices, museums and festival dates, so check those before booking.

items.name: Konoba Scala Santa (Kotor Old Town)
items.detail: Most consistently recommended in the guides I found. One guide calls it Kotor's oldest restaurant, and Fodor's mentions lobster, mussels and fresh fish. Fills up quickly, so book ahead in season.

photo.credit: Klavs / CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

items.name: Galion
items.detail: Harbour-side restaurant. One guide says Tripadvisor ranked it number one in Kotor at the time. Fodor's describes it as sophisticated, with creative twists on local food. Check current ratings.

items.name: Konoba Akustik
items.detail: Just outside the old town walls, overlooking the bay and river. One writer says it covers the staples of the local menu.

items.name: Pržun
items.detail: Fodor's calls it Kotor's most romantic restaurant.

items.name: Marenda Grill House
items.detail: Meat-focused grill just outside the old town. Fodor's rates it for locally sourced meat and its popularity with locals.

items.name: Heritage Grand Perast by Rixos
items.detail: Hotel in an 18th-century palace in UNESCO-listed Perast, with a spa, hammam and sauna. Scored 9.4/10 on Expedia in the listing I saw.

items.name: Vila Perast Boutique Hotel
items.detail: About a five-minute walk from Smekja Palace and St Nicholas' Church. Terrace and garden.

items.name: Hotel Libertas, Prčanj
items.detail: 18th-century stone house with a private beach area, outdoor pool and sea-view rooms. A reviewer praised the quiet location.

items.name: Boutique Hotel Astoria Kotor
items.detail: Inside the old town, in the 14th-century Buca Palace. A good base if you want to stay within the walls.

items.name: Kotor Carnival
items.detail: A winter carnival with a masked parade through the city. A summer edition has run for about 20 years, opening with a Fisherman's Feast in the Square of Arms. I did not find current dates.

items.name: Our Lady of the Rocks tradition
items.detail: Legend dates the island to 1452. Sailors dropped stones around the chapel before a voyage, a tradition that built the islet up. The church holds 68 paintings by the baroque artist Tripo Kokolja.

items.name: Kotor Old Town and fortress walls
items.detail: The medieval walled town and its fortifications are the core sight.

photo.credit: User:Ggia / CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons
photo.alt: Kotor Old Town and fortress walls

items.name: Our Lady of the Rocks, Perast
items.detail: Man-made island with a chapel, usually reached by boat. Perast itself is a baroque waterfront town.

photo.credit: FrDr / CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons
photo.alt: Our Lady of the Rocks, Perast

items.name: San Giovanni Fortress
items.detail: Reached by the Ladder of Kotor, a climb of roughly 1,350 steps. Sources disagree on the fee (one says €8, 8am-8pm, May-September; another says early climbs are free). Check before you go.

photo.credit: Diego Delso / CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

items.name: Climb the Ladder of Kotor
items.detail: An old caravan trail that once linked Kotor with Cetinje. An early start avoids crowds and heat.

photo.credit: kallerna / CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

items.name: Boat trip to Our Lady of the Rocks and the Blue Cave
items.detail: Boat tours run from the bay to the island and the Blue Cave.

items.name: Day trip to Perast and Prčanj
items.detail: Both are within about 12 km of Kotor by road, and Perast can also be reached by sea.

items.name: Currency and costs
items.detail: Montenegro uses the euro (from my own knowledge, not a search result). I did not find current price levels, so check costs before you go.

items.name: Getting around
items.detail: Tivat to Kotor is about 15-20 minutes through the Vrmac tunnel, and a taxi is quoted at roughly €25-30 (from a low-quality guide). Check taxi fares locally.

items.name: Passport rules
items.detail: Your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before entry and expire at least three months after you leave.

bestTime: I did not find a verified source in this research. Late spring and early autumn are generally milder and quieter than peak summer, but check a current climate guide.
gettingThere: Fly to Tivat (about 3h10 from Manchester; fares roughly €70-290 per Rome2Rio, with limited days) or Dubrovnik, which is a longer drive with a border crossing. Check current timetables.
travelAdvice: The FCDO page was last updated on 13 August 2026, per a mirror of gov.uk rather than gov.uk itself. The update added wait times for travel to and from the Schengen area and updated road-travel and swimming-safety information. Land borders can close at short notice. Check gov.uk before travelling.
